claims.text: Anthropic recommends starting agent evals with 20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures and grading outcomes rather than paths.
pass^k measures the probability that all k trials succeed; a 75% per-trial success rate gives about 42% pass^3.
Meta diffs landed via RADAR had a revert rate about one-third that of non-RADAR diffs and a production-incident rate about one-fiftieth that of non-RADAR diffs (observational, not causal).
Anthropic found that generator self-evaluation fails because agents confidently praise their own mediocre work; a separate evaluator is easier to tune toward skepticism.
Uber's uReview comments are rated useful 75% of the time, and 65% of them are addressed in the same changeset.
ImpossibleBench found that hiding test files reduces reward hacking to near zero but significantly degrades legitimate performance.
